steps.title: Prepare HSAEC culture medium
steps.instruction: Formulate 506.75 mL complete growth medium under sterile conditions, keep dark at 2–8 °C, use within 30 days.

substeps.instruction: Transfer airway epithelial cell basal medium (485 mL) to a sterile container.

Add Bronchial Epithelial Growth kit components to achieve final concentrations: HLL supplement 500 µg/mL, Linoleic acid 0.6 µM, Lecithin 0.6 µg/mL, L‑glutamine 6 mM (1.25 mL), Airway epithelial cell supplement 15 mL, Epinephrine 1.0 µM, Transferrin 5 µg/mL, T3 10 nM, Hydrocortisone 5 µg/mL, rhEGF 5 ng/mL, rh insulin 0.1 µg/mL.
Add optional penicillin‑streptomycin solution (Pen 10 U/mL, Strep 10 µg/mL, 0.5 mL).
Mix to a final volume of 506.75 mL, filter‑sterilize if required, and store in the dark at 2–8 °C (do not freeze).

steps.title: Prepare 70 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Mix 72.9 mL 96 % ethanol with 27.1 mL ultrapure sterile water to obtain 100 mL of 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Initiate HSAEC culture
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen cells, combine with pre‑warmed complete medium, seed, and establish initial culture.

substeps.instruction: Check vial label for cell number; select a T‑flask (T25, T75, etc.) to achieve 5,000–10,000 cells/cm².
Calculate medium volume (3–5 mL per 25 cm²) and transfer to a sterile tube; warm to 37 °C (20–30 min for 50 mL).
Lightly mist vial, tube, and flask surfaces with 70 % ethanol; keep all items inside the biosafety cabinet.
Thaw cryovial in a 37 °C water bath for 1–2 min; do not exceed this time.
Transfer the thawed suspension to the pre‑warmed medium with a sterile pipette and mix gently (do not centrifuge).
Add the entire suspension to the selected flask and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, 20 % O₂ for 24 h.
After 24 h, inspect under a microscope; if attachment is insufficient, incubate an additional 12–14 h.
Prewarm fresh complete medium to 37 °C, aspirate old medium carefully, and replace with fresh medium.
Return flask to incubator; assess confluency after 24–48 h and aim for ~90 % confluency before further steps.

steps.title: Passage HSAEC cells
steps.instruction: Detach, collect, and reseed cells using trypsin‑EDTA and neutralizing solution.

substeps.instruction: Warm complete medium, trypsin‑EDTA (0.05 % trypsin, 0.02 % EDTA) and trypsin neutralizing solution to 37 °C; let D‑PBS reach room temperature.
Aspirate culture medium from the flask without disturbing cells.
Rinse the cell layer with 3–5 mL D‑PBS and aspirate completely.
Add 2 mL pre‑warmed trypsin‑EDTA per 25 cm², rock gently, and incubate at 37 °C for 1–3 min.
Observe under a microscope; if cells remain attached, tap the flask bottom firmly. Do not use a scraper. If needed, incubate an additional 1–2 min (max total 5 min).
Neutralize trypsin by adding an equal volume of neutralizing solution, mix gently.
Transfer the suspension to a sterile centrifuge tube; rinse the flask 2–3 times with 5 mL D‑PBS and combine all fractions.
Centrifuge at 150 × g for 5 min, aspirate supernatant, and resuspend pellet in 1–3 mL pre‑warmed complete medium (start with 1 mL for small pellets).
Mix 10 µL cell suspension with 10 µL 0.4 % Trypan Blue, load 10 µL onto a dual‑chamber counting slide, and determine viable cells per mL.
Based on the count, either seed a larger flask (150–300 cm²) for expansion or proceed to ALI culture.

steps.title: Prepare ALI inserts
steps.instruction: Sterilize tools, place ThinCert inserts into 24‑well plates, and set up humidity container.

substeps.instruction: Collect and count cells as described in the passage step.
Calculate number of inserts needed (0.1 × 10⁶ cells per insert; target density ≈3.0 × 10⁵ cells/cm²).
Disinfect tweezers by submerging in 5–10 mL 70 % ethanol (in a 15 mL tube) for 5–10 min; air‑dry completely.
Using sterile tweezers, transfer each Greiner Bio‑One ThinCert (0.4 µm, 24‑well) into the wells of a 24‑well plate; avoid edge wells—fill edge wells with 1 mL sterile water to maintain humidity.
Place the plate(s) in a lidded plastic container together with an open 15 mL tube containing 2–3 mL sterile water; keep the lid slightly ajar and incubate.

steps.title: Seed cells in liquid‑liquid culture
steps.instruction: Add cells to inserts and medium to wells; maintain for 7 days with bi‑daily medium changes.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 0.1 × 10⁶ cells suspended in 400 µL complete medium into the interior of each insert.
Add 1 mL complete medium to the well beneath each insert.
Include one insert without cells as a blank control for TEER.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, 20 % O₂, humidified for 7 days.
Replace medium every 48 h: 400 µL into each insert and 1 mL into the corresponding well.

steps.title: Establish ALI culture
steps.instruction: Remove apical medium, add basal medium, and maintain humidity; change medium every 48 h.

substeps.instruction: After 7 days, carefully aspirate medium from both wells and inserts without disturbing the cell layer.
Add 270 µL complete medium to the well beneath each insert (bottom of insert should be just submerged).
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, 20 % O₂, humidified.
Change the basal medium every 48 h, maintaining ~270 µL; if medium accumulates inside the insert, remove excess and adjust the basal volume accordingly.
Avoid air bubbles under the insert; keep the plastic container with plates and the water tube in the incubator, lid slightly open.

steps.title: Monitor ALI culture
steps.instruction: Keep plates in incubator and measure TEER weekly.

substeps.instruction: Maintain plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, 20 % O₂, humidified.
Replace basal medium every 48 h as described.
Measure transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER) at least once per week (more often if needed).

steps.title: Prepare TEER measurement
steps.instruction: Prewarm medium, disinfect and condition electrode, and calibrate the TEER meter.

substeps.instruction: Prewarm the required volume of complete medium to 37 °C (temperature consistency is critical).
Submerge the electrode in 5–7 mL 70 % ethanol for 2–3 min, then air‑dry completely.
Condition the electrode by submerging it in 5–7 mL pre‑warmed complete medium, then air‑dry.
Adjust electrode height so the longer arm reaches the bottom of the well and the shorter arm does not touch the insert membrane; set this height once and keep it constant.
Power on the Millicell TEER unit, insert the test electrode, and verify the display reads 1,000 Ω; adjust manually if necessary.
Plug the measurement electrode in, wait a few minutes for stabilization, then proceed to measurement.

steps.title: Replace medium for TEER
steps.instruction: Add fresh medium to inserts and wells, then equilibrate temperature before reading.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate medium from the well.
Add 400 µL of pre‑warmed complete medium to each insert and 1 mL to the corresponding well.
Incubate the plate in the incubator for 15 min, then place it outside the biosafety cabinet for an additional 15 min to allow temperature equilibration.

steps.title: Measure TEER resistance
steps.instruction: Record baseline and sample resistances, then clean the electrode.

substeps.instruction: Immerse the electrode (short arm inside the insert, long arm in the well) in the blank insert; keep it vertical (90°) and avoid touching insert edges.
Allow the reading to stabilize (~1 min) and record the baseline resistance.
Repeat the measurement for each cell‑covered insert, obtaining at least two independent readings per well; average the values.
After all measurements, immerse the electrode in 70 % ethanol for 2–3 min and air‑dry.

steps.title: Calculate TEER value
steps.instruction: Compute NET resistance and multiply by insert surface area (0.33 cm²) to obtain Ω·cm².

substeps.instruction: NET resistance = (Resistance of cell‑covered insert) – (Resistance of blank insert).
TEER (Ω·cm²) = NET resistance (Ω) × insert surface area (cm²).
Example: 350 Ω (cells) – 280 Ω (blank) = 70 Ω; 70 Ω × 0.33 cm² = 23.1 Ω·cm².

description: Validation of protocol Since TEER values are closely linked to tight junction expression, the presence of ZO-1, claudin-1, and claudin-4 was assessed on days 12 and 21 using western blot. Representative results are shown in Figure 6 . Figure 6. Visualisation of tight junction proteins (ZO-1, claudin-1, and claudin-4) in human small airway epithelial cell (HSAEC) cultures maintained under air–liquid interface (ALI) conditions for 12 and 21 days. Western blotting was performed using ZO-1, claudin-1, claudin-4, and β-actin antibodies at a 1:1,000 dilution, in accordance with established protocols [10].
